title: Pushing the Same Way
endLine: Compensation moves the other term the same way, never past 7.40.

scenes.tts: Plasma p H follows one ratio. The lungs keep its bottom; the kidney keeps its top. When a disturbance pushes one term, what does the other keeper do?
scenes.narration: Plasma pH follows one ratio. The lungs keep its bottom; the kidney keeps its top. When a disturbance pushes one term, what does the other keeper do?
scenes.caption: Plasma pH follows one ratio. The lungs keep its bottom; the kidney keeps its top. When a disturbance pushes one term, what does the other keeper do?
scenes.visual: Continue the first film's 16:9 world and colour map without a reset. COLOUR BY CONCEPT, as before: bicarbonate BLUE fluid and dots; dissolved carbon dioxide ORANGE fluid and bubbles; acid RED dots; pH gauge and needle bright WHITE; lungs PINK; kidney PURPLE. LAYOUT, as before: CENTRE, filling about 70% of frame height, the two clear tanks stacked as a fraction on one shared hidden scale (50 mmol/L full), BLUE 'bicarbonate' above a thick WHITE fraction bar, ORANGE 'dissolved CO2' below, fluid heights always in proportion to concentration. LEFT: PINK lungs joined to the lower tank, PURPLE kidney joined to the upper tank. RIGHT: the vertical pH gauge, 6.0 to 7.6, bright tick at 7.40, needle ALWAYS computed as 6.1 + log10(upper level / lower level). NEW this film: a WHITE readout under the lungs, 'pCO2 40 mmHg', and the tag 'human plasma, 37 C' at bottom right. Opening at rest: 24 over 1.2, '20 : 1' on the fraction bar, needle at 7.40, lungs swelling slowly, BLUE dots drifting. On 'lungs keep its bottom', the lungs and lower tank pulse; on 'kidney keeps its top', the kidney and upper tank pulse. On 'pushes one term', a RED plug at the bottom of the upper tank pops open for a moment and the BLUE level twitches down, then the plug closes and the level recovers. On the question, white text across the top: 'What does the other keeper do?'
Title 'Pushing the Same Way' fades in across the top for 2 s while the question text fades out. The world rests at 24 over 1.2, needle at 7.40; lungs keep swelling slowly; BLUE dots drift.

scenes.tts: If carbon dioxide moves first, the disturbance is respiratory. If bicarbonate moves first, it is metabolic. Take a metabolic acidosis: bicarbonate falls from twenty-four to twelve.
scenes.narration: If carbon dioxide moves first, the disturbance is respiratory. If bicarbonate moves first, it is metabolic. Take a metabolic acidosis: bicarbonate falls from 24 to 12.
scenes.caption: If carbon dioxide moves first, the disturbance is respiratory. If bicarbonate moves first, it is metabolic. Take a metabolic acidosis: bicarbonate falls from 24 to 12.
scenes.visual: On 'respiratory', the label 'respiratory' appears beside the lower tank and the lungs pulse. On 'metabolic', the label 'metabolic' appears beside the upper tank and the kidney pulses. On 'metabolic acidosis', the 'respiratory' label fades and a tag 'made-up patient' appears at bottom left and stays all film. On 'falls from twenty-four to twelve', the RED plug opens and the BLUE fluid drains steadily from 24 to 12 (label counts '24' down to '12'), then the plug closes. During the drain the lungs are held at 'pCO2 40 mmHg' and the needle slides down, computed.

scenes.tts: Dissolved carbon dioxide is zero point zero three times its pressure. At forty millimeters of mercury, that is one point two. Hold it there, and the ratio drops to ten to one. p H would fall to seven point one.
scenes.narration: Dissolved CO2 is 0.03 times its pressure. At 40 mmHg, that is 1.2. Hold it there, and the ratio drops to 10 to 1. pH would fall to 7.1.
scenes.caption: Dissolved CO2 is 0.03 times its pressure. At 40 mmHg, that is 1.2. Hold it there, and the ratio drops to 10 to 1. pH would fall to 7.1.
scenes.visual: On 'zero point zero three', a WHITE line appears beside the lower tank: '0.03 x 40 = 1.2', joining the 'pCO2 40 mmHg' readout to the thin ORANGE layer (label '1.2'). On 'hold it there', a small clamp icon sits on the lung tube and the lungs keep their resting rate. On 'ten to one', the fraction-bar label reads '12 : 1.2 = 10 : 1'. On 'seven point one', the needle settles at 7.10 (6.1 + log10 10), label '7.10, no help'. A faint WHITE ghost tick stays at 7.10 on the gauge for the rest of the film.

scenes.tts: But within minutes, breathing begins to deepen, and carbon dioxide falls too. It reaches its full extent over about twelve to twenty-four hours. Both terms fall, so the ratio climbs back toward twenty.
scenes.narration: But within minutes, breathing begins to deepen, and carbon dioxide falls too. It reaches its full extent over about 12 to 24 hours. Both terms fall, so the ratio climbs back toward 20.
scenes.caption: But within minutes, breathing begins to deepen, and carbon dioxide falls too. It reaches its full extent over about 12 to 24 hours. Both terms fall, so the ratio climbs back toward 20.
scenes.visual: The clamp icon lifts. A stopwatch icon by the lungs, label 'minutes'. On 'deepen', the lungs swell deeper and faster and ORANGE bubbles stream out of the lower tank through them; the readout begins counting down from 40. On 'twelve to twenty-four hours', the stopwatch morphs into a clock face labelled '12 to 24 hours'. On 'both terms fall', a BLUE down-arrow appears beside the upper tank and an ORANGE down-arrow beside the lower tank, both labelled 'down'. The ORANGE layer thins and the needle climbs up off the 7.10 ghost tick (computed from the levels).

scenes.tts: In this made-up patient, carbon dioxide settles at twenty-seven millimeters of mercury. That leaves zero point eight one dissolved. Twelve over zero point eight one is fourteen point eight. Its log is one point one seven, so p H is seven point two seven.
scenes.narration: In this made-up patient, carbon dioxide settles at 27 millimeters of mercury. That leaves 0.81 dissolved. 12 over 0.81 is 14.8. Its log is 1.17, so pH is 7.27.
scenes.caption: In this made-up patient, carbon dioxide settles at 27 millimeters of mercury. That leaves 0.81 dissolved. 12 over 0.81 is 14.8. Its log is 1.17, so pH is 7.27.
scenes.visual: The readout stops at 'pCO2 27 mmHg'; the lungs keep breathing at their new deeper rate. The ORANGE layer settles at 0.81 on the hidden scale, label '0.81' (the line beside it now reads '0.03 x 27 = 0.81'). The fraction-bar label reads '12 : 0.81 = 14.8 : 1'. The needle settles at 7.27, label '7.27', above the 7.10 ghost tick and below the 7.40 tick. On 'its log is one point one seven', a WHITE line under the gauge reads '6.1 + 1.17 = 7.27' as the needle settles.

scenes.tts: Full repair would mean twenty to one again. With bicarbonate at twelve, how low would carbon dioxide need to fall, in millimeters of mercury?
scenes.narration: Full repair would mean 20 to 1 again. With bicarbonate at 12, how low would CO2 need to fall, in mmHg?
scenes.caption: Full repair would mean 20 to 1 again. With bicarbonate at 12, how low would CO2 need to fall, in mmHg?
scenes.visual: A dashed WHITE target line runs across the gauge at 7.40, label 'full repair'. The '20 : 1' label reappears, dashed, above the fraction bar. The readout under the lungs shows '27' with a blinking WHITE '?' beside it. White question card across the top: 'For 20 : 1, pCO2 = ?'
Predict pause. The question card stays. Near-stillness by design: the lungs keep their deep rhythm, ORANGE bubbles trickle out, the needle trembles at 7.27, the '?' blinks slowly.

scenes.tts: To twenty millimeters. Twenty to one, with twelve on top, needs zero point six dissolved. Divide by zero point zero three: twenty. The lungs stopped at twenty-seven. They bought back about zero point one seven of a p H unit, but not all of it.
scenes.narration: To 20 millimeters. 20 to 1, with 12 on top, needs 0.6 dissolved. Divide by 0.03: 20. The lungs stopped at 27. They bought back about 0.17 of a pH unit, but not all of it.
scenes.caption: To 20 millimeters. 20 to 1, with 12 on top, needs 0.6 dissolved. Divide by 0.03: 20. The lungs stopped at 27. They bought back about 0.17 of a pH unit, but not all of it.
scenes.visual: Question card dissolves. On 'to twenty', a dashed ORANGE ghost level appears in the lower tank at 0.6 (0.03 x 20), labelled 'needs 20 mmHg'; the real ORANGE layer stays at 0.81, labelled '27'. On 'bought back', a WHITE bracket on the gauge spans the 7.10 ghost tick to the needle at 7.27, label '0.17 bought back'. On 'not all of it', a dashed bracket spans 7.27 to the 7.40 target line, label 'not all'. As the working is spoken, a WHITE line builds beside the lower tank: '12 ÷ 20 = 0.6', then '0.6 ÷ 0.03 = 20 mmHg'.

scenes.tts: Here is the one idea. Compensation moves the other term in the same direction as the first. The ratio heads back toward twenty, usually partway. Sometimes, in chronic respiratory disorders, it gets nearly all the way. It never carries p H past seven point four.
scenes.narration: Here is the one idea. Compensation moves the other term in the same direction as the first. The ratio heads back toward 20, usually partway. Sometimes, in chronic respiratory disorders, it gets nearly all the way. It never carries pH past 7.4.
scenes.caption: Here is the one idea. Compensation moves the other term in the same direction as the first. The ratio heads back toward 20, usually partway. Sometimes, in chronic respiratory disorders, it gets nearly all the way. It never carries pH past 7.4.
scenes.visual: The ghost level and brackets fade. On 'same direction', the BLUE down-arrow and the ORANGE down-arrow return beside the tanks and pulse together, joined by a WHITE label 'same way'. On 'usually partway', the needle at 7.27 glows. On 'nearly all the way', a faint ghost needle rises to just under 7.40 and fades, tag 'some chronic cases'. On 'never carries p H past', the dashed 7.40 target line becomes a solid WHITE wall, label 'never past 7.40'. The lungs keep their deep rhythm; the real needle stays at 7.27.

scenes.tts: For metabolic acidosis, Winter's formula expects one and a half times bicarbonate, plus eight, give or take two. One and a half times twelve, plus eight, is twenty-six. So twenty-four to twenty-eight is expected, and twenty-seven fits. It is a line fitted to people, with scatter, not a law.
scenes.narration: For metabolic acidosis, Winter's formula expects 1.5 times bicarbonate, plus 8, give or take 2. 1.5 times 12, plus 8, is 26. So 24 to 28 is expected, and 27 fits. It is a line fitted to people, with scatter, not a law.
scenes.caption: For metabolic acidosis, Winter's formula expects 1.5 times bicarbonate, plus 8, give or take 2. 1.5 times 12, plus 8, is 26. So 24 to 28 is expected, and 27 fits. It is a line fitted to people, with scatter, not a law.
scenes.visual: Beside the readout under the lungs, a short vertical WHITE scale of pCO2 (20 to 40 mmHg) slides in. On 'Winter's formula', a line builds above it: '1.5 x 12 + 8 = 26'. On 'give or take two', a shaded WHITE band from 24 to 28 lights on the scale, label 'expected'. On 'twenty-seven fits', a marker at 27 drops into the band and gets a tick; the 20 mark for full repair sits visibly below the band. On 'fitted to people', a loose cloud of small WHITE dots scatters around the band, tag 'schematic scatter'; label 'a fit, not a law'. The '1.5 x 12 + 8 = 26' line builds as 'one and a half times twelve, plus eight' is spoken, and '26 ± 2' appears under it on 'give or take two'.

scenes.tts: When carbon dioxide rises first, the kidney is the keeper that answers. Take a rise from forty to fifty. At once, the blood's other buffers add about one millimole per litre of bicarbonate. Over days, as the kidney makes new bicarbonate, the rise reaches about five, in one study. Full repair needs twenty times one point five: thirty, six more.
scenes.narration: When carbon dioxide rises first, the kidney is the keeper that answers. Take a rise from 40 to 50. At once, the blood's other buffers add about 1 millimole per litre of bicarbonate. Over days, as the kidney makes new bicarbonate, the rise reaches about 5, in one study. Full repair needs 20 times 1.5: 30, 6 more.
scenes.caption: When carbon dioxide rises first, the kidney is the keeper that answers. Take a rise from 40 to 50. At once, the blood's other buffers add about 1 millimole per litre of bicarbonate. Over days, as the kidney makes new bicarbonate, the rise reaches about 5, in one study. Full repair needs 20 times 1.5: 30, 6 more.
scenes.visual: The Winter scale slides out. Reset smoothly to rest (24 over 1.2, readout 40, needle 7.40, plug closed); the 'made-up patient' tag changes to 'illustrative: pCO2 40 to 50'. On 'carbon dioxide rises first', the lungs slow and shallow, ORANGE bubbles stop leaving, the readout climbs to 50, the ORANGE layer rises to 1.5 and the needle drops (computed, no number shown); an ORANGE up-arrow appears by the lower tank. On 'at once, buffering', the BLUE level rises from 24 to 25, label '+1 at once'. On 'over days, the kidney', a calendar icon labelled 'days' appears, the kidney glows PURPLE, BLUE dots flow from it into the upper tank and the level rises to 29, label '+5 over days'; a BLUE up-arrow appears beside the ORANGE one, 'same way'. The needle climbs to just under 7.40 (computed from 29 over 1.5). On 'full repair would need six', a dashed BLUE ghost line at 30 appears just above the fluid, label '+6 for full'. The '+1 at once' label reads '+1 at once: other blood buffers'. On 'twenty times one point five', a WHITE line by the lower tank reads '0.03 x 50 = 1.5', then a line by the upper tank '20 x 1.5 = 30', as the dashed BLUE ghost line at 30 appears. Cue changes: 'at once, buffering' is now 'at once, the blood's other buffers'; 'over days, the kidney' is now 'over days, as the kidney'; 'full repair would need six' is now 'twenty times one point five'.

scenes.tts: So read a blood gas against this rule. Numbers moving in opposite directions, or a compensation far off the fit, mean two things are going on at once.
scenes.narration: So read a blood gas against this rule. Numbers moving in opposite directions, or a compensation far off the fit, mean two things are going on at once.
scenes.caption: So read a blood gas against this rule. Numbers moving in opposite directions, or a compensation far off the fit, mean two things are going on at once.
scenes.visual: Schematic only, no numbers. On 'opposite directions', the two arrows beside the tanks flip so that one points up and the other down; they flash against each other and a WHITE label appears between them: 'two processes'. Then they return to pointing the same way. On 'far off the fit', a small ghost of the Winter band appears by the lungs with a ghost marker sliding well outside it, label 'off the fit'. On 'two things', both labels pulse once together, then fade.

scenes.tts: So the lungs answer a metabolic push, and the kidney answers a respiratory one. Each pulls p H back toward seven point four, and neither overshoots.
scenes.narration: So the lungs answer a metabolic push, and the kidney answers a respiratory one. Each pulls pH back toward 7.4, and neither overshoots.
scenes.caption: So the lungs answer a metabolic push, and the kidney answers a respiratory one. Each pulls pH back toward 7.4, and neither overshoots.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the full world. On 'the lungs answer a metabolic push', the scene briefly shows the metabolic case again (BLUE at 12, lungs breathing deep, ORANGE at 0.81, two down-arrows, needle at 7.27). On 'the kidney answers a respiratory one', it morphs to the respiratory case (ORANGE at 1.5, kidney glowing, BLUE at 29, two up-arrows, needle just under 7.40). On 'neither overshoots', the solid WHITE wall at 7.40 pulses and both needle positions sit below it.

End card over the dimmed but still moving world (lungs breathing, ORANGE bubbles leaving, BLUE dots drifting, the WHITE wall at 7.40 on the gauge). Large white text, centred: 'Compensation moves the other term the same way, never past 7.40.'
